Conditions raised by RiskMap

Source: R/conditions.R
riskmap_conditions.Rd

Errors, warnings and messages from RiskMap carry classes, so that code can handle them with tryCatch() or withCallingHandlers() without matching their text, which may be reworded between versions.

  • riskmap_error is the class of every error that RiskMap raises on purpose. A more specific class says what went wrong.

    • riskmap_error_input, an argument has a value that the function can't use. The field arg of the condition names the argument.

    • riskmap_error_fit, a model can't be fitted or a computation on a fit fails, for example because the search for the mode of the latent effects fails or every Monte Carlo weight is zero.

    • riskmap_error_worldpop, WorldPop can't be reached or has no data for the request.

    • riskmap_error_internal, a problem in RiskMap itself. Please report it.

  • riskmap_warning is the class of every warning.

    • riskmap_warning_fit, a fit may not be reliable, for example because the optimiser did not converge or the Monte Carlo error of the estimate is not certified.

    • riskmap_warning_crs, the projected coordinate reference system used distorts distances by more than 1% over the data (see propose_crs() and crs_distortion()).

  • riskmap_message is the class of every message. Functions that report on their progress take an argument messages, whose default is the option RiskMap.messages, so that options(RiskMap.messages = FALSE) silences them all.

Examples

# Which argument was rejected
tryCatch(
  get_worldpop("Liberia", 2020),
  riskmap_error_input = function(condition) condition$arg
)
#> [1] "country"
